audio_forensics.recording_starts: mid-sentence, inside Dwyer's opening remarks; appearance announcements NOT on the tape
audio_forensics.preprocessing: 16 kHz mono; high-pass 70 Hz; low-pass 7.6 kHz; 1-second-window AGC; soft limiter; normalise -3 dBFS. Average level raised 6.7x from -40 dBFS.

asr.settings: beam 5, best_of 5, temperature fallback, word timestamps, Silero VAD, domain-primed prompt
asr.parallelism: split at silences (996.9 / 1962.0 / 2882.5 s), two workers concurrent (4 GB each; four OOM'd)
asr.result: 1068 segments, 0.00-3874.48 s, mean segment log-prob -0.180, zero segments below -0.6

diarisation.problem: Both principal speakers are men with median F0 136 Hz on one distant mic. Pure neural embedding clustering FAILED - it separated by segment length, not speaker.
diarisation.breakthrough: The AGC had erased the strongest cue. On the ORIGINAL audio the bench sits at -41 dB and the bar table at -53 dB - a 12 dB mic-distance gap.
diarisation.final_method: Viterbi over three evidence streams: (1) acoustic - Resemblyzer GE2E on un-normalised audio, PCA-32, centroids seeded from utterances only one person could make ('the appellant' = reading the pleading; 'my manager' = the Appellant); (2) lexical - ~60 weighted patterns; (3) adjacency - a question drops the switch penalty to 15%, and certain openings prove the PREVIOUS segment was the other speaker.
diarisation.reliability: Turn structure reliable. Residual errors concentrated in one- and two-word interjections and overlapping speech. NOT CERTIFIED.

response_latency.reading: He answered as fast as the bench. Not the profile of a witness constructing answers. This is the strongest single fact the audio produced.

outlier.reading: Longest silence in the hour by a factor of four. He was reading his own index to locate item 10 - he had handed up his only copy. Document-searching, not hesitation. Looks identical on paper, which is why the audio matters.

the_tell.finding: Three of his five highest-pitched utterances are HEDGES - 'I do believe that I have received those' (+4.5 st), 'I do believe we have those' (+3.6 st), 'I would have to triple check' (+3.3 st).
the_tell.contrast: 'No, I have all of that' at 9.7 w/s - three times baseline, flat, instant - disposed of Stressor 3.
the_tell.rule: When he knows, he is fast and flat. When he does not, his pitch rises and broadcasts it. In the box: say 'I'd have to check' at baseline pitch, short, and stop.
